SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.

REPORT

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. & S. B. REGISTRY.
S. I. S. D. Station,
No. D 75
Date April 19 1933
**〔此处转录不清：右上角手写批注及划线〕**

Subject (in full) Circular Order for Arrest of one Deo Thien-yih (程天一)

Made by ____________________ and ____________________ Forwarded by Superintendent Robertson

This is an automatic issue of a circular order
following an unsuccessful attempt to execute a warrant for
the arrest of the defendant issued at the instance of the
Bureau of Public Safety. It is alleged by the Bureau that
Doo, a former employee of the South Manchurian Railway, has
received sums of money from Japanese sources for the purpose
of engineering insurrection or otherwise embarrassing the
Nanking Government. A few days after the unsuccessful
attempt to execute the original warrant at the Burlington
Hotel, members of the Bureau of Public Safety endeavoured,
without the cooperation of the Municipal Police, to make
enquiries as to Doo's whereabouts at a house on Yu Yuen Road,
near Bubbling Well Police Station - they were not certain
as to the number. These activities **〔此处转录不清：涂改痕迹〕** however were cut
short by C.I. Maguire who informed the officers of the Public
Safety Bureau that they must adhere to the proper procedure
by first seeking the assistance and cooperation of the
Municipal Police.

Enquiries at the Burlington Hotel elicited the
information that Doo had been a guest there on and off for
some time back and there is nothing to indicate that he
was a bona fide resident of the Settlement.

The document is quite in order and in the event
of its execution it is the duty of the Municipal Police to
see that extradition proceedings are regular.

I attach file relating to the unsuccessful attempt
to execute the original warrant at the Burlington Hotel.

Thos Robertson
Superintendent.

Officer i/c Special Branch

报告

上海公共租界工部局警务处
刑事与特别股登记处。
特务股分站，
D 75号
日期 1933年4月19日
**〔此处转录不清：右上角手写批注及划线〕**

事由（全称） 关于逮捕程天一（Deo Thien-yih）的通缉令

由 ___ 和 ___ 制作，经罗伯逊（Robertson）警司转发

这是一份自动签发的通缉令，
此前因执行公共安全局申请签发的针对
被告的逮捕令未果而发出。据公共安全局指控，
杜（Doo），前南满洲铁道株式会社雇员，
收受来自日本方面的款项，旨在策划叛乱
或以其他方式使南京政府陷入困境。在
伯灵顿酒店（Burlington Hotel）执行原逮捕令
失败几天后，公共安全局成员试图在没有
工部局警务处合作的情况下，在靠近静安寺
巡捕房的愚园路（Yu Yuen Road）一处住宅
查询杜的下落——他们不确定门牌号码。
这些活动 **〔此处转录不清：涂改痕迹〕** 然而被麦圭尔（Maguire）首席督察制止，
他告知公共安全局官员，他们必须遵守
正当程序，即首先寻求工部局警务处的
协助与合作。

对伯灵顿酒店的查询显示，杜在过去
一段时间内曾断断续续地作为客人入住该处，
且没有任何迹象表明他是租界的合法居民。

该文件完全符合规定，若予以执行，
工部局警务处有责任确保引渡程序正规。

随函附上关于在伯灵顿酒店执行原逮捕令
未遂的相关卷宗。

托马斯·罗伯逊（Thos Robertson）
警司。

特务股主管警官
**〔此处转录不清：左侧边缘多处手写签名及日期“19/4”〕**

先生，供阅知。

File No. 4107
(C. & S.B.) Office Notes April 4, 1932.
Execution of Search Warrant No. 4107
In conjunction with representatives of the Public
Safety Bureau, detectives searched Room No. 305, in the
Burlington Hotel, Bubbling Well Road occupied by one Doo Tien
I'h (杜天一) between 5 p.m. and 6 p.m. on March 31, 1932 but
nothing incriminating was found nor was the occupant located.
A watch was kept at the Burlington Hotel until 2.30p.m.
on April 1, 1932 but as Doo Tien I'h (杜天一) did not return it
was discontinued.
Search Warrant No. 4107 returned herewith.
P. A., Crime.
C.I. White,
Shanghai Special District Court.

执行搜查令第4107号
1932年3月31日下午5时至6时之间，侦探
会同公共安全局代表，搜查了位于静安寺路
伯灵顿酒店、由杜天一（Doo Tien I'h）占用的
305号房间，但未发现任何罪证，也未找到
占用者。
在伯灵顿酒店进行了监视，直至1932年
4月1日下午2时30分，但因杜天一（Doo Tien I'h）
未返回，遂停止监视。
现退回搜查令第4107号。
P. A.，犯罪科。
怀特（White）首席督察，
上海特区地方法院。

Between 5 p.m. and 6 p.m. the 31/3/32, D.S. Golder, representatives of the Public Safety Bureau, C.D.S.I. Huang and the undersigned, acting on the authority of Search Warrant No. 4107, issued by Judge Chow of the S.S.D. Court at the request of the Public Safety Bureau searched room No. 305 in the Burlington Hotel, Bubbling Well Road, occupied by one named Doo Tien I'h (杜天一) but nothing incriminating was found and the above man was not located there. A watch was kept in the Burlington Hotel by a representative of the Public Safety Bureau and C.D.C.'s until 2.30 p.m. the 1/4/32 for the possible return of the above named Doo Tien I'h (杜天一) but he did not appear and therefore the Guard was withdrawn.

Search Warrant No. 4107 attached herewith.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S. 1. Station
REPORT
Date April 1, 1932.
Subject (in full) Re execution of warrants no.4106 & 4107 issued by the Shanghai
Special District Court at the instance of the Public Safety Bureau.
Made by D.S. Golder Forwarded by **〔此处转录不清：手写签名〕**

Enquiries at the Burlington Hotel, Bubbling Well
Road on March 30 showed that the property is registered at
the British Consulate under the name of Mr. J. Burke. In
view of this a visit was paid to the residence of Mr. Haines,
No.12 Peking Road, with the object of having the warrants
officially countersigned. He, on examination of the
documents stated that that he could on no account sign either
of them until he had consulted with the Consul-General.
In explanation of his refusal Mr. Haines stated that it was
contrary to the existing law to allow a search to be made
for seditious literature or anything of a political nature
concerning another nation or country in the home of or on
the premises of a British subject. On the following day,
however, Mr. Haines after a consultation with H.M. Judge,
intimated that, Mr. J. Burke was only an employee of the
owner who is a Chinese. A visit was therefore paid to
the address designated in the attached warrant at 5 p.m.
March 31st, when it was learned that Doo Tieh i'h (杜天一)
had not been seen there since 11.25 p.m. on the preceding
day. No luggage was found in the room whilst 'Doo' owes
the Hotel something in the region of $1,000.00.

**〔此处转录不清：手写签名〕**
D. S.

Officer i/c Special Branch.

日期 1932年4月1日。
事由（全称） 关于执行上海特区地方法院应公共安全局之请求签发的第4106号和4107号令状。
由侦探警士戈尔德（Golder）制作，经 **〔此处转录不清：手写签名〕** 转发

3月30日对静安寺路伯灵顿酒店的查询显示，
该物业以J. Burke先生的名义在英国领事馆注册。
鉴于此，走访了位于北京路12号的Haines先生住所，
目的是对令状进行正式副署。他在审查文件后表示，
在与总领事协商之前，他绝不能签署其中任何一份。
为解释其拒绝原因，Haines先生指出，允许在
英国臣民的家中或寓所内搜查煽动性文献或涉及
另一国家或政治性质的物品，违背现行法律。
然而次日，Haines先生在与H.M. Judge协商后，
告知J. Burke先生仅为业主（一名中国人）的雇员。
因此，于3月31日下午5时前往附呈令状中指定的
地址，得知自前一天晚上11时25分以来，无人见过
杜天一（Doo Tieh i'h）。房间内未发现行李，而
‘杜’欠酒店约1,000.00美元。

**〔此处转录不清：手写签名〕**
D. S.

Burlington Hotel.
Wanted by the Shanghai Public
Safety Bureau for being a
reactionary.

In conjunction with a representative of the
Bureau of Public Safety, an attempt was made by
Detective Sergeant Golder to execute this warrant
at 5 p.m. March 31, when it was learned that Doo
Tieh-i'h had not been seen in the Burlington Hotel
since the previous evening and that he, Doo, owes
the hotel something in the region of $1,000.

Superintendent.

Inspector White.
